Not built - needs a maintainer look (new dependencies, and a code conflict with main).

I read the complete diff and issue #3874. I did not build this PR: it declares two dependencies the maintainer has not confirmed (`libc` on Unix and `windows-sys` on Windows, in `crates/app/Cargo.toml`, with `Cargo.lock`), and it cannot go to the runner either (the author is not a collaborator with push access, and the runner refuses a PR that touches a `Cargo.toml`). I also could not build locally (no C toolchain on this machine), which agrees with the not-built reading.

The dependency decision is recorded in `docs/decisions/3874-ui-link-transport.md` (the `interprocess` crate was dropped; the pipe is written against `windows-sys`); the maintainer still has to confirm the two declarations.

What looks good:
- The redesign is reasoned: the named pipe with a user-only ACL on Windows, the kernel-reported server process id as the peer proof before one byte of the token crosses, pid liveness before a stale file is removed, one elapsed deadline over the whole hello exchange, capped answer lines and a bridge bound that fails a truncated session.
- The pinned tests cover the false pipe, the TCP refusal, the slow peer, the oversized line and the bridge bound.
- New modules carry provenance lines; the files stay under 400 lines.

Results: not built. No suite was run. The body's readings (11 ui_link tests, app lib 307, clippy clean) are not verified here.

Conflicts with main (code, not ledger): `crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs`, `crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs`, `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs`, `crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs`. Main merged PR #3883 (JSwetz) on 2026-11-25T05:41Z - a different fix for the same issue #3874: loopback TCP plus a mutual token proof (SipHash-2-4) plus answer line limits. This PR replaces the same functions with the named-pipe transport and a raw token, and deletes the token-proof scheme. Merging this over main would overwrite #3883 with a competing design. Neither side is an append-only ledger, so no local resolution is safe.

Requested before merge:
1. Maintainer decision on the two dependencies (`libc` on Unix, `windows-sys` on Windows in `crates/app/Cargo.toml`), or drop them. Docs: `docs/decisions/3874-ui-link-transport.md`.
2. Maintainer decision on the design: #3874 is already closed by #3883. Either drop/close #3971, or merge `origin/main` and reconcile the two implementations (one hello, one link_client, one test suite) with fresh green tests of the refreshed head. The body's `Fixes #3874` cannot close anything (the issue is closed).
3. A fresh green review of the refreshed head, with a real build, before any merge.

Notes (not blocking):
- `hello_matches` now checks the raw token in constant time instead of a proof. That is the redesign's stated point and is recorded in the decision record; the trade-off is that the token now crosses the socket on Unix (same user, 0700 folder).
- `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs` is 398 lines - one over the 400-line rule is a note, not a blocker. `crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs` grew to 692 lines (a test file, but worth a look).
- The `"pipe"` transport is `cfg(windows)` only. No Windows run here; the pipe transport and its tests are unexercised on this machine.
- The `--ui mcp` bridge's end-of-stdin note (a pipe cannot close one direction) is recorded in the decision record as a known limit.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
